_readme: Agent-researched resolutions of the needs-review queue (official pages fetched 2026-08-07; every non-unclear record carries a verbatim quote). Consumed when regenerating the overlays; hand-reviewed before applying.

geo.evidence: Enrolled member of a U.S. Federally-recognized American Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Corporation
geo.note: Eligibility is tribal-enrollment based; page states no state residency or state-school requirement. Active (2026-27 app opens Dec 15, 2026).

geo.evidence: Must be a graduating senior at a high school in DC, MD, or VA, ​OR have graduated high school within three (3) years and not yet started college and reside in DC, MD, or VA
geo.note: Must also plan to enroll full-time at a college in DC, MD, or VA. Household income caps apply ($74,800-$141,000 by household size). Next cycle opens May 1, 2027.

geo.evidence: Yes. Our scholarship is open to all states in the U.S. including Puerto Rico.
geo.note: Active; current deadline March 6, 2026.

geo.evidence: Applicants must be a resident of Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington but may study elsewhere.
geo.note: Residency-bound but school may be anywhere. No citizenship check, consistent with who.

geo.evidence: Enroll in an accredited technical school, college, or university as a full-time undergraduate
geo.note: Tribal enrollment documentation (self or parent) required; no state restriction stated. 2026-27 application open.

geo.evidence: Every year, thirteen (13) $25,000 scholarships are awarded to students based on academic success, community service and financial need.
geo.note: Official page and FAQ state no geographic eligibility rule; detailed rules moved behind the Scholarship America Hub login (learnmore.scholarsapply.org/cfacommunityscholars redirects there). The US/PR/Canada residency in `who` could not be verified on a public official page.

geo.evidence: Reside in a qualifying rural North Carolina county
geo.note: Also requires NC residency for tuition purposes and enrollment at a participating North Carolina public or private college/university; 26 qualifying rural counties (PDF list). Reopens January 2027.

geo.evidence: Reside within New York State
geo.note: Current NY residency is the stated bound.

geo.evidence: In order to be eligible, you must reside in Horizon Farm Credit's territory, made up of the following states/counties: Delaware, Maryland (Baltimore, Carroll, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery,
geo.note: Territory: all DE and PA, 16 MD counties, VA counties (Accomack, Clarke, Frederick, Northampton, Page, Shenandoah, Warren), WV counties (Berkeley, Brooke, Hancock, Jefferson, Marshall, Morgan, Ohio), and Washington D.C. 2027 apps open Sept 18, 2026.

geo.evidence: seniors in high school planning to attend a college or university in the next academic year in IL, IN, IA, KS, MI, MN, MO, NE, ND, OH, SD or WI
geo.note: Per official rules: legal residents of any of the 50 states or DC may apply, but the school attended (or planned) must be in the 12 listed states, per the school-in-state bound. 2026 application period closed; landing page has no eligibility text.

geo.evidence: Attending four-year colleges and community colleges in the U.S. and Puerto Rico
geo.note: Page shows a 3.0 GPA floor; the 2.8-vs-3.0 conflict in `who` was not visible in the fetched eligibility section.

geo.evidence: You are a resident of the fifty states, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico (see questions 14 and 15).
geo.note: US-wide inclusiveness, not a state bound. Must also live AND attend school in the 50 states/DC/PR. Main page 403-walls fetchers; verified via browser on the official FAQ page. 2027 application opens in December.

geo.evidence: permanent residents within CA, IL, NY, or TX
geo.note: Landing page lacks eligibility text; rule is on the General Program Information subpage.

geo.evidence: Be an Arkansas resident (at least 12 months prior to enrollment and a US citizen/lawful permanent resident)
geo.note: Must also attend an approved Arkansas institution of higher education.

geo.evidence: With the exception of financial need, the student must meet all other PA State Grant eligibility requirements to qualify for RTSS.
geo.note: PA State Grant eligibility includes Pennsylvania residency; students must be nominated by an approved participating (Pennsylvania) institution, and the program is funded by the Pennsylvania General Assembly. Page is JS-walled to fetchers; verified via browser.

geo.evidence: Degree-seeking students must be attending an accredited institution full-time in the U.S.
geo.note: General eligibility is Tribal-affiliation based (TEC required) with no state bound. Some individual named funds in the finder (e.g., PNM Pueblo, Shakopee Mdewakanton) carry their own tribal/regional criteria. Scholarship-finder URL is a JS tool and 403-walls fetchers; verified via browser on official FAQ.

geo.evidence: U.S. Citizens, Nationals, and Lawful Permanent Residents; b. Who are sophomore or junior-level students of accredited higher education institutions;
geo.note: No state restriction in the official 2026 Eligibility Criteria PDF (main page carries no eligibility text). Native categories additionally require enrollment in a federally recognized tribe.

geo.evidence: the College of Education at Mississippi State University (MSU) and the School of Education at the University of Mississippi (UM)
geo.note: Bound is by institution: scholars must enroll at MSU or Ole Miss (both in Mississippi). Residency is NOT restricted - overview says the program is designed to attract students from Mississippi 'as well as surrounding states'. Five-year MS public-school teaching commitment with repayment terms per `who` not restated on fetched pages.

geo.evidence: Students from across the nation apply.
geo.note: Semifinalists travel to Clarinda, Iowa for the in-person finals at their own expense - travel requirement, not a residency bound. Active, 2026 deadline April 20.

geo.evidence: Reside in the United States or Puerto Rico
geo.note: US/PR-wide inclusiveness, not a state bound; must also attend an accredited US or PR institution and be an active ABC-USA church member.

geo.evidence: be a United States or Canadian citizen
geo.note: General awards have no state bound. Arizona quirks exist: permanent residents may apply only from Arizona, AZ applicants may carry 9 credit hours, and there is a separate Arizona financial-need scholarship - consistent with `who`.

geo.evidence: apply to one or more of our partner schools. If you qualify, you'll automatically be considered for a Stamps award.
geo.note: Eligibility runs through partner institutions nationwide; no state residency restriction (institution-specific deadlines may differ for in-state vs out-of-state applicants).

geo.evidence: Both full-time and part-time employees in the United States, Canada and Puerto Rico are eligible.
geo.note: Employment-based (current Chick-fil-A Team Member), no state bound. Also open in Canada.

geo.evidence: The Chafee Grant may be used at any eligible California college or university, or career or technical school. Students attending schools in other states may also qualify.
geo.note: California state program (CSAC/California Dept. of Social Services) for current/former California foster youth (ward of the court, in care at least one day between ages 16-18, under 26). School may be outside California - the bound is qualifying through California's foster-care system. Batch URL 405-walls fetchers; verified via browser, which redirects context to csac.ca.gov/chafee.

geo.evidence: Two student leaders from each state, the District of Columbia and the Department of Defense Education Activity
geo.note: Every state participates via its own state selection administrator; delegates travel to Washington Week - not a residency bound to specific states.

geo.evidence: Applicants must live in Oregon, or the following counties in Washington State: Klickitat or Yakima.
geo.note: Washington eligibility limited to Klickitat and Yakima counties. 2026 deadline passed (Jan 10, 2026); page says check again next year.

geo.evidence: a farmworker or child of a farmworker who has been employed by a California Farm Labor Contractor (FLC) within the past 12 months
geo.note: Bound is employment through a California farm labor contractor rather than residency. 2027 application opens Spring 2027.

geo.evidence: The program's information has moved to a new location
geo.note: learnmore.scholarsapply.org/toyotamle now only shows a moved notice pointing to the Scholarship America Hub, where the Toyota Motor North America Scholarship Program page requires account login (verified via browser). The 14-states+DC+PR rule in `who` could not be confirmed on a public official page.

geo.evidence: Enroll full-time in Build Dakota Scholarship-eligible program at a South Dakota technical college (Lake Area Technical College, Mitchell Technical College, Southeast Technical College, or Western Dakota Technical College).
geo.note: No residency requirement stated (out-of-state students may apply); bound is attending an SD technical college plus the FAQ commitment: 'Following graduation, work full-time in South Dakota in the field of study for a minimum of three years.' Apply page has no eligibility text; rule is on the FAQ page.

geo.evidence: scholarships to Alaska Natives who are Sealaska Shareholders and Descendants
geo.note: Eligibility is Sealaska shareholder/descendant status (lineage-based); page states no residency requirement, so 'in Southeast Alaska' in `who` reflects the corporation's region rather than a stated residency rule. Individual named awards may add criteria.

geo.evidence: Westchester Community College, Dallas College, City Colleges of Chicago, Colorado Community College System – Aurora, Denver and Front Range campuses, Valencia College, Los Angeles Community College – LA Trade Tech and LA City College
geo.note: Bound is current attendance at one of the named partner campuses in these six states. Program currently closed; page says 2026 program information is tentative and subject to change.

geo.evidence: Applicants must be current high school juniors or seniors at the time of application and must reside in the United States.
geo.note: US-wide legal residency only, no state bound ('only legal residency in the United States is required to participate'). Application period currently closed. Site 403-walls fetchers; verified via browser FAQ accordion.

geo.evidence: all of Kentucky's public 4 (year) universities as well as all the colleges and institutions of the Kentucky Community and Technical College System (KCTCS)
geo.note: For youth committed to Kentucky's Cabinet for Health and Family Services, aged out of Kentucky foster care at 18+, or adopted from Kentucky's system; waiver usable only at Kentucky public institutions, must start within 4 years of HS/GED, up to 150 credit hours or age 28.

geo.evidence: All regular full- and part-time and limited part-time permanent Costco employees residing in the United States and Puerto Rico may be eligible
geo.note: US-or-Puerto-Rico inclusiveness, no state restriction.

geo.evidence: You are a legal resident of New York State and have resided in New York State for 12 continuous months.
geo.note: Also requires attending SUNY or CUNY and graduating from a NYS high school in the top 10 percent.

geo.evidence: Meet TOPS Louisiana Residency requirements
geo.note: Usable only at Louisiana institutions (LCTCS campuses, Louisiana public colleges, or LAICU member private colleges).

geo.evidence: enrolled in a two-year or four-year program at eligible South Carolina institutions
geo.note: Qualifies through South Carolina's system: page states the program offers financial assistance to members of the South Carolina Army and Air National Guard; no separate residency sentence on the page.

geo.evidence: a qualifying member of the national guard who enrolls in an accredited postsecondary institution in North Dakota which is not controlled by the state may receive a grant
geo.note: ND National Guard benefit (state system). Contradiction with who-sentence: N.D.C.C. 37-07.2-01.1 now also allows grants at out-of-state and online institutions, and this chapter covers non-state-controlled ND institutions, not only ND state schools.

geo.evidence: enrolled or intend to enroll at an eligible institution in an undergraduate or graduate program leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate
geo.note: Maryland residency is NOT required ('Applicants are no longer required to be Maryland residents'), but the program must be at an eligible Maryland institution with a Maryland teaching commitment, so the award is MD-bound.

geo.evidence: All out of state members of an American Indian nation, tribe and pueblo, located wholly or partially in New Mexico, regardless of the residence of the member prior to acceptance at a post-secondary educational institution shall be eligible to pay the in-state tuition rate.
geo.note: Benefit is in-state tuition at New Mexico public institutions; qualifies through NM tribal ties, not current residency.

geo.evidence: Scholarships available to undergraduate engineering or pre-engineering students who are enrolled full-time in a post-secondary educational institution and pursuing a Bachelor of Science or Engineering degree
geo.note: Eligibility routes are accreditation-based (ASHRAE student branch, ABET, Washington/Sydney Accord). A few named awards give 'special consideration' to ASHRAE Region III schools, but that is a preference, not a residency bound.

geo.evidence: Reside in PG&E's service territory, or Be a dependent of a resident in PG&E's service territory
geo.note: PG&E's service territory is in California. Contradiction with who-sentence: per the page, territory residency is required of all applicants; the HBCU option is only an alternative for where the student enrolls ('a four-year college or university in California or a Historical Black College or University (HBCU) in the U.S.'), not an alternative to residency.

geo.evidence: Recipients must be a member of a federally recognized American Indian Tribe or Alaska Native village.
geo.note: Eligibility is tribal-membership-based (Preparatory/Pre-Graduate tracks also allow state-recognized or terminated tribes and descendants); no state restriction.

geo.evidence: Participants must live and work in Minnesota.
Youth who are age-eligible for 4-H participation must be actively enrolled in the Illinois 4-H program at the time of application to qualify for this scholarship.
geo.note: Qualifies through Illinois 4-H membership ('Open to current Illinois 4-H members age 15-19').

geo.evidence: Residency is defined as the veteran's full-time physical presence in a Louisiana household.
geo.note: Main page states 'Eligibility for Title 29 education benefits also require that veterans meet residency requirements' and links this residency-requirements PDF; benefit is a Louisiana in-state tuition exemption tied to the veteran's one-year Louisiana residency.

geo.evidence: enrolled members of certain Indigenous American Tribal Nations
geo.note: Quote is from the Kansas Board of Regents FAQ answer stating 'Kansas law allows in-state tuition rates for individuals including ... enrolled members of certain Indigenous American Tribal Nations' at state universities. The FAQ does not name the four Kansas-headquartered tribes listed in the who-sentence; it defers to K.A.R. 88-3-11.

geo.evidence: Our CPF scholarship program awards scholarships to outstanding planning students enrolled at eligible professional planning degree programs in California
geo.note: Bound by enrollment in California planning programs; no separate residency rule stated.

geo.evidence: Must be currently enrolled as a full-time student in good standing at a CVTEA-accredited veterinary technology, veterinary nursing, or animal health technology program in the United States or Puerto Rico.
Undergraduates attending a community college, university or technical institution outside of Florida
geo.note: General Application Fund is an exclusion, not a state bound: undergraduates may attend anywhere in the US EXCEPT Florida (Florida undergrads are served by the separate James S. Davis fund); full-time graduate students have no geographic restriction stated. Consistent with the who-sentence.

geo.evidence: Be a Missouri resident and a United States citizen or permanent resident
geo.note: Also requires enrollment in a participating Missouri postsecondary school.

geo.evidence: enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate teacher education program at an eligible Nebraska institution
geo.note: Also requires commitment to teach full-time in an accredited or approved public or private school in Nebraska, matching the who-sentence's forgivable-loan terms.

geo.evidence: enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate teacher education program at an eligible Nebraska institution
geo.note: Student-teaching variant; also requires the Nebraska full-time teaching commitment ('teach full-time in an accredited or approved public or private school in Nebraska').

geo.evidence: Either listed Indiana as home of record at the time of enlistment in the armed forces of the United States OR resided in Indiana at least five (5) years before the student first applies
geo.note: Veteran parent must have the Indiana connection; benefit is usable at Indiana public colleges (and capped $5,000 at Indiana private nonprofits).

geo.evidence: Qualifying programs must directly relate to one of the high-need occupations and must be offered at a qualifying North Dakota institution.
geo.note: Recipients also agree to 'Live within ND for 3 years following program completion' and 'Work in an in-demand occupation within ND for 3 years following program completion.' Page fetched via curl (site has an SSL-chain issue that blocks some fetchers).

geo.evidence: Graduate from an accredited South Dakota high school with a Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.8 or greater on a 4.0 scale.
geo.note: Original URL is only an application-timeline page with no eligibility text; resolved via the SDBOR knowledge-base eligibility article, which also requires attending 'a participating South Dakota college' and agreeing 'to stay in South Dakota and work in a critical need occupation after graduation.'

geo.evidence: Graduation from an accredited South Dakota high school
geo.note: Must also 'attend a public or non-public accredited university, college or technical institute located in South Dakota.'

geo.evidence: the governing board of each institution shall adopt a policy to grant in-state tuition classification to a student who is a registered member of a federally recognized American Indian tribe with historical ties to Colorado
geo.note: C.R.S. 23-7-112; benefit is Colorado in-state tuition classification at Colorado public institutions (Fort Lewis College excluded due to its existing tuition waiver). Page fetched via curl after a 403 to the default fetcher.

geo.evidence: Be a certified peace officer currently employed by a Utah law enforcement agency
geo.note: Also must be 'Seeking a post-secondary degree in a criminal justice-related program from a credit-granting USHE institution' (Utah System of Higher Education).

geo.evidence: Scholarship recipients must be residents of the state of Oklahoma as determined by the State Regents.
geo.note: Also must be 'enrolled full time in an undergraduate program at a public or private college or university in the state of Oklahoma.'

geo.evidence: Any public institution of higher education, as defined in TEC, Section 61.003(8), is required to participate in the Children of Disabled or Deceased Firefighters and Law Enforcement Officers program.
geo.note: THECB guidelines PDF (extracted locally; page serves the PDF). Parent must have served as a firefighter, municipal/county/state peace officer, state game warden, or paid TDCJ custodial officer 'in the state of Texas'; exemption applies at Texas public institutions.

geo.evidence: Any public institution of higher education as defined in TEC, Section 61.003, is required to participate in the Education Benefits for Certain Survivors of Individuals in Specific Public Servant Positions program.
geo.note: The exemptions/waivers page lists this program's guidelines as 'Under Construction', so the THECB guidelines PDF (TEC 54.354) was used. Qualifying public servants are those of 'this state or of a political subdivision of this state' (Texas agencies, TDCJ, etc.); exemption applies at Texas public institutions.

geo.evidence: provides an exemption from tuition and laboratory fees to eligible persons employed as firefighters by a political subdivision of the state of Texas or active members of an eligible organized volunteer fire department in this state
geo.note: THECB guidelines PDF (TEC 54.353), extracted locally. Eligible institutions are 'Texas public institutions as defined in TEC, Section 61.003.'

geo.evidence: You are a legal resident of New York State and have resided in New York State for 12 continuous months.
geo.note: Also requires 'Pursuing an undergraduate degree at a participating NYS private college.' Program is active (2026-27 deadline listed).

geo.evidence: You are a legal resident of New York State and have resided in New York State for 12 continuous months.
geo.note: Also 'Available to students pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree or in an approved vocational training program in New York State.'

geo.evidence: You are a legal resident of New York State and have resided in New York State for 12 continuous months.
geo.note: Also requires 'Study at an approved post-secondary institution in New York State.'

geo.evidence: Study at an approved post-secondary institution in New York State.
geo.note: Attendance at an approved NYS institution is required. Non-NYS residents (including undocumented students) must first qualify under the NYS DREAM Act, so residency alone is not the bound - study in NY is.

geo.evidence: Have been in the care and custody of New Jersey Department of Children and Families Child Protection & Permanency in an out-of-home placement for a cumulative of 9 months or more following the youth's 16th birthday.
geo.note: All qualifying categories run through NJ CP&P placement, NJ CP&P adoption/KLG, or NJ-approved independent/transitional living programs. State Tuition Waiver portion is usable only at NJ public schools; ETV funds follow the student.

geo.evidence: for any dependent child of a (A) police officer, as defined in section 7-294a, or supernumerary or auxiliary police officer, (B) firefighter, as defined in section 7-323j, or member of a volunteer fire company
geo.note: Statute directs each board to 'waive the payment of tuition' at Connecticut public institutions (community-technical colleges under 10a-77, CSU under 10a-99, UConn under 10a-105) for dependents of officers/firefighters killed in the line of duty; officer definitions are Connecticut statutory ones. cga.ct.gov has a TLS certificate-chain issue; text retrieved from the same official URL via direct download.

geo.evidence: Physically reside in Massachusetts for at least one year, as of the start of the enrolled term, with an intent to remain in Massachusetts consistent with Board of Higher Education policy
Physically reside in Massachusetts for at least one year, as of the start of the enrolled term, with an intent to remain in Massachusetts consistent with Board of Higher Education policy
geo.note: Page is the Foster Child Grant: also requires being 'placed in the custody of the Department of Children and Families through a Care and Protection Petition' (MA DCF), so both residency and custody bounds are Massachusetts.

geo.evidence: Physically reside in Massachusetts for at least one year, as of the start of the enrolled term, with an intent to remain in Massachusetts consistent with Board of Higher Education policy
geo.note: Also requires enrollment in an approved licensure program at a Massachusetts 4-year public institution; service/repayment terms in the who-sentence match the page.

geo.evidence: Physically reside in Massachusetts for at least one year, as of the start of the enrolled term, with an intent to remain in Massachusetts consistent with Board of Higher Education policy
geo.note: Page states a two-year Commonwealth public-school teaching commitment ('Commit to teaching for two (2) years in a public school in the Commonwealth upon successful completion of a bachelor's degree'); the who-sentence's one-year-per-waiver-year phrasing differs slightly - worth syncing.

geo.evidence: in an undergraduate program of study leading to a certificate or an associate degree in an approved course of study at a public community college in Massachusetts
geo.note: Also carries the standard one-year Massachusetts physical-residency requirement.

geo.evidence: Be enrolled in the 10th or 11th grade in a public or private secondary school in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
geo.note: Also requires physically residing in Massachusetts with intent to remain.

geo.evidence: in a program leading to a certificate, associate, or bachelor's degree at any public postsecondary institution within the state shall not be required to pay tuition or mandatory fees for attendance at such institution
geo.note: Qualification runs through New Hampshire DCYF foster care/custody/guardianship categories and the waiver applies only at NH public institutions (CCSNH/USNH), consistent with the who-sentence's under-26 and 35-recipient caps.

geo.evidence: Each CCSNH College will provide annually a $500 scholarship for up to 12 scholarships in high schools in its region for students who successfully complete the NH Scholars Program.
geo.note: Award qualifies through the New Hampshire Scholars Program at NH high schools and is usable only at the awarding CCSNH college (not transferrable), valid one year after graduation.

geo.evidence: Commit to working in Vermont, as a healthcare professional in a healthcare setting, serving a rural community (minimum of 32 hours per week), for 5 years following completion of your degree and receipt of your license (if applicable)
geo.note: Vermont residency NOT required (non-VT residents considered if funding allows); the bound is the 5-year Vermont work commitment — carried by basis.service-commitment, not geo.

geo.evidence: Agree to work full-time in Vermont in your profession for a minimum of one year for each year of funding received
geo.note: Page: 'Vermont residency is not required'; the bound is the required Vermont work commitment — carried by basis.service-commitment, not geo.

geo.evidence: Enrolled full-time at the following institutions only: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore
geo.note: Also requires being 'Determined to be eligible for in-state tuition by the institution' and ROTC membership. Page lists both full-time and part-time student categories, so the who-sentence's blanket full-time rule may be overstated.

geo.evidence: Be a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen (as determined by the institution) and enroll at an eligible, regionally accredited, public or independent Florida postsecondary institution.
geo.note: 2025-26 fact sheet frames initial funding only for 'A student who is a Florida resident' (with narrow Florida-diploma exceptions for home education or military/public-service families away from Florida); the former out-of-state National Merit pathway does not appear. All recipients must attend a Florida institution.

geo.evidence: Be a legal resident of the State of Mississippi for one year prior to application.
geo.note: Also: 'Recipients must attend one of Mississippi's public two-year colleges or public four-year universities.' Matches the who-sentence including the automotive-industry essay.

geo.evidence: Be a Missouri resident and a United States citizen or permanent resident
geo.note: Also requires enrollment at 'a participating Missouri postsecondary school' and the officer must be 'employed by Missouri or a political subdivision of the state'.

geo.evidence: Must be accepted to a Kansas nursing program (pre-nursing will not be funded);
geo.note: Kansas residency is explicitly NOT required per KBOR's state-aid brochure, but recipients must attend a Kansas nursing program and 'work full-time as an RN or LPN one year for each year that scholarship assistance was received in the state of Kansas'; unmet service repays at 5% interest, matching the who-sentence.

geo.evidence: This program is only available at Kansas State University, Pittsburg State University, University of Kansas, Wichita State University, and Washburn University.
geo.note: Brochure: 'Student agrees to accept a commission as a Second Lieutenant and serve for not less than four years as a commissioned officer in the Kansas Army National Guard.' Brochure lists Washburn University, matching the who-sentence.

geo.evidence: Be a nontraditional student attending, or planning to attend, an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school in the United States
geo.note: Page: 'Applicants from the state of Indiana are encouraged to apply' - encouragement only, no state restriction. Applications currently closed; 2026 info tentative. Page says HS graduation year 2021 or prior (who-sentence says 2020 or earlier - update).

geo.evidence: Must have ancestral roots or heritage from the Dominican Republic.
geo.note: No state or geographic restriction on the page; supports students of Dominican descent pursuing higher education in the United States. natddp.org is the National Dominican Day Parade, not the Dominican American National Roundtable (DANR) named in the who-sentence - the attribution should be corrected. Full guidelines PDF referenced for additional criteria.

geo.evidence: Be a current consumer of the KY Office of Vocational Rehabilitation with an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE).
geo.note: No separate residency line, but eligibility runs entirely through Kentucky's state vocational-rehabilitation system, matching the who-sentence.

geo.evidence: To be eligible, a student's legal guardian must be a full-time employee of an MBA member station.
geo.note: No student residency requirement stated; the bound operates through Massachusetts Broadcasters Association member radio/TV stations (Massachusetts-licensed), so students themselves could live out of state.

geo.evidence: Applicant must be a graduate of or have attended a DoDEA high school.
geo.note: Host organization is the Nevada State Education Association, but the page states no Nevada residency or NSEA membership requirement for this scholarship; DoDEA high schools exist worldwide, not in any one state.

geo.evidence: A graduating senior from each of the following counties will be selected to receive a $5,000 Board of Director's scholarship: Abbeville, Anderson, Cherokee, Colleton, Darlington, Dorchester, Fairfield, Greenville, Greenwood, Jasper
geo.note: Quote truncated for length - the full county list ends ', Marlboro, and McCormick.' All eligible counties are in South Carolina and rotate each cycle; the separate 2026 Presidential Scholarship goes to a Chesterfield County (SC) resident. Matches the who-sentence.

geo.evidence: Be enrolled or planning to enroll in a full-time undergraduate course of study at one of the following CME Group Foundation partner schools for the entire upcoming academic year
geo.note: 13 partner schools listed: 12 in Illinois plus Stevens Institute (Hoboken, NJ), matching the who-sentence. Applications currently closed.

geo.evidence: permanent residents of one of the counties or municipalities listed (can attend school at any location)
geo.note: Eligible counties: DE - Kent, New Castle; NJ - Atlantic, Burlington, Camden, Cape May, Cumberland, Gloucester, Mercer, Salem; PA - Berks, Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Lehigh, Montgomery, Northampton, Philadelphia. School may be anywhere. Applications currently closed; 2026 info tentative.

geo.evidence: Preference is given to applicants planning to work in the Midwest—Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, South Dakota or North Dakota.
geo.note: Midwest work plans are a stated PREFERENCE, not a requirement; hard requirements are free MSSA membership, enrollment in an accredited program at a nonprofit institution (no state named), a declared health/human-services major, and one semester remaining. Landing page at /scholarships loads, but detail pages sit behind a Cloudflare JS wall for plain fetchers (retrieved via rendering browser).

geo.evidence: Have experience working with (via field practicum, paid employment, or volunteer experience) or plan to work with children and/or families in Minnesota.
geo.note: No residency or in-state-school rule; the Minnesota nexus is required experience with / plan to work with children and families in Minnesota — a work-plan bound, not geo.

geo.evidence: Preference is given to applicants planning to work in the Midwest—Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, South Dakota or North Dakota.
geo.note: Midwest work plans are a stated PREFERENCE, not a requirement; hard requirements are MSSA membership and enrollment in an accredited health/human-services program at a nonprofit institution (no state named). Covers both undergraduate ($2,500 x2) and graduate ($3,000 x3) awards.

geo.evidence: Each year, since 1989, the Township Officials of Illinois Scholarship Fund awards funds to graduating high school seniors to continue their education at Illinois colleges/universities.
geo.note: The page itself states only the Illinois colleges/universities bound; detailed criteria (including the Illinois residency and citizenship rules in the who-sentence) live in the downloadable application, not on the page.

geo.evidence: High school senior from Wilmington attending a New Castle County high school and planning to enroll in a 2-year or 4-year college, or trade/vocational school
geo.note: Listing (Dr. Joseph P. Pyle Award, deadline March 19, 2026) is also tagged 'Delaware Residents Only'. Wilmington and New Castle County are in Delaware.

criteria.quote: Applicants must have financial need

eligibility.evidence: Be current high school seniors residing in one of the 50 U.S. states, District of Columbia or Puerto Rico who plan to enroll full-time in an accredited two- or four-year college or university
eligibility.note: No niche field/identity/circumstance criteria; page carries an explicit nondiscrimination statement. Employees and immediate family of Equitable or Scholarship America are ineligible. Consistent with who.

criteria.quote: Demonstrate financial need.

eligibility.evidence: Current college undergraduates who have completed at least one year of full-time undergraduate study ... Be studying to obtain their first Associate's or first Bachelor's degree.
eligibility.note: Page confirms 'high school seniors are not eligible' — consistent with who (second year or later). Open to all fields; a separate STEM award category exists but the general award has no field restriction.

criteria.quote: original research in critically important scientific fields of study and full application for holistic review
original research in critically important scientific fields of study and full application for holistic review

eligibility.evidence: Unique among high school competitions, the Regeneron STS focuses on identifying, inspiring, and engaging the nation's most promising future leaders in STEM.
eligibility.note: It is a research competition requiring submission of an original STEM research project. Full Official Rules PDF exceeded fetch size limit; quotes are from the official program homepage.

criteria.quote: Students with a Korean heritage studying in the United States regardless of citizenship status (including Korean Nationals).

eligibility.evidence: Undergraduate, graduate and high school students enrolled full time during the scholarship application year.
